parole.significato: Any of several wild geese, of the genus Branta, that breed in the Arctic, but especially the brent goose, Branta bernic…
parole.testo: From New Latin/Medieval Latin Branta, latinized form of Old Norse brandgás (“sheldrake”), literally "burnt (black) goose," from Proto-Germanic *brandaz (“burning”) + *gans (“goose”).

parole.testo: From Latin Fennī; compare Ancient Greek Φίννος (Phínnos). The name as used by Tacitus is unclear about whom it actually describes, but it may nevertheless be from Old Norse Finnr (“a Sami”). More at Fenni.

parole.significato: The feast of Passover or (specifically) the Paschal Lamb, or (for Christians), Easter, seen as the fulfillment of Passo…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin pascha. Perhaps also influenced by Old Norse páskar and its derivatives.

parole.significato: An abode of the gods or afterlife in general.
parole.testo: From New Latin, from Old Norse Valhǫll (from valr (“dead warriors”) + hǫll (“hall”)).
